newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV says refining, marketing to help 97 profit.
newsitem.headline: OMV says refining, marketing to help 97 profit.

text.p: Austrian oil group OMV said on Tuesday it expects earnings in 1997 to match last year's record as improved refining margins and a stronger market performance offset the impact of lower crude oil prices.
Chief executive Richard Schenz told a news conference he "expected a similar result for 1997 as 1996".
In 1996 OMV posted a net profit of 1.98 billion schillings, a pre-tax profit of 2.97 billion and earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of 2.92 billion.
Marketing was "on the right track for higher earnings" this year in the face of further cost-cutting measures in Austria and expansion in Eastern Europe, Schenz said.
Last year marketing achieved an operating profit of 0.12 billion schillings after a 1995 loss of 0.06 billion.
Lower crude oil prices had already boosted refining margins by around 10 percent to $2 a barrel based on Rotterdam prices, director Tassilo Peyrer-Heimstatt said.
"But I don't expect a significant improvement over the $2 a barrel without a consolidation in European refining," he added.
Refining EBIT fell to 0.12 billion schillings last year from 0.62 billion in 1995.

Schenz forecast a profit in exploration and production (E&P) this year, despite a recent slump in the price of benchmark Brent crude. On Tuesday Brent was quoted a shade above $17.5 a barrel, well below the 1996 average of $20.7.
"We have budgeted for a Brent crude price of $17.50 this year. And at the moment it looks as though we may not be too far wide of the mark," Schenz said.
Last year OMV's E&P division rebounded to post a 0.25 billion schillings EBIT after a 0.39 billion loss in 1995.
Schenz said he expected gas earnings to remain stable around last year's 1.77 billion schillings.

Plastics and chemicals profits would suffer from an expected downturn in the second half of the year, Schenz said. He did not expect a significant decline from 1996 EBIT of 0.51 billion schillings in plastics and 0.5 billion in chemicals, however.
